armed.text: A door in a row of doors, and this is the one with the sign. PLEASE KNOCK, in a careful hand, the letters evened out with a ruler. Underneath, smaller: I AM USUALLY IN. The frame is scored with six deep gouges at chest height, all of them arriving from the same direction, and the gouges have rust in them that is not from the rebar. Someone has knocked. Several someones.

choices.label: Back off the step, slow, without touching the door
Find the spring and take the tension off it

escaped.text: You go backwards down the step with your hands where the door can see them, which is idiotic, and you keep doing it anyway until there is a street between you and the sign. Behind you the house waits to be knocked on. It is very good at waiting.

cache_1.text: It is a garage spring off a roller door, wound to about nine hundred newtons and tethered to a metre of reinforcing bar filed to a chisel. You get a screwdriver into the sear and let it down by degrees, and when it finally goes slack the whole house seems to exhale. The hall beyond is neat. Shoes lined up. A little tray for keys, with keys in it.

choices.label: Go through to the back room the hall is pointing at

cache_2.text: The back room holds the pantry, and the pantry holds more than one person could eat in a season, which is the first clue. The second is on the floor beside it, under a second rebar arm on a second spring: what is left of a careful, ruler-using, shoe-lining-up someone, one arm still stretched out toward the shelf, fingers closed on a tin. They forgot their own second door. {{irony}} You step around them and take the tin. It seems rude to leave it.

the_courtesy.text: Your heel finds the loose board on the step — the one the whole thing was actually listening for — and the door opens for you. The rebar comes out of the dark at chest height and you get your pack into it, mostly, and the rest of it goes through the meat above your hip and out again with a sound like a boot coming out of mud. The door closes politely behind it.

the_knock.text: The sear slips. Nine hundred newtons of garage spring discover you at the exact moment you discover them, and the filed end of the bar goes in under the collarbone and comes out through the back of the shoulder, and for a long stupid second you and the rebar look at each other. Then it retracts. It retracts. You had not considered that it would need to reset.

the_second_courtesy.text: There was a second spring. It has been holding its breath since before the pantry was full, and it lets go with a noise like a struck bell. You are wearing the doorframe when it happens, which is the only reason you are still wearing your face.

irony: They were, to the last, extremely considerate.
They did knock. That was the arrangement.
The sign was for them too, in the end.
Nobody is good at their own front door.
